ledger.contains: EDB annual report FY2020/21. In scope: infographic (p. 11) and text on real estate (pp. 12-13): projects approved under PDS (10), Smart City (3), IHS (2) and NRP (6, not a residence route); 286 residential acquisition authorisations worth MUR 10.3 billion (already in data); 25 business-property authorisations (MUR 1.25 bn, not a residence route); 2021/22 budget measures on IRS/RES/PDS/IHS/G+2 (rules legislated in FA 2021, taken from that Act). Work and live section (pp. 31-33): 2020/21 changes (permit validity 3 to 10 years, investor minimum USD 100,000 to 50,000, PRP investment USD 500,000 to 375,000, already recorded from FA 2020); Table 4 active OP/RP holders 30 June 2021 (investor 918, retired 758 already in data; professional 4,347 and self-employed 431 and total 6,454 out of scope); 5,138 dependants and 427 PRP holders (already in data); Table 5 permits grandfathered to 10 years (investor 764, retired 668 added; self-employed 358 out of scope); Figure 9 nationalities of all active OP/RP holders (8 shares added, mixed categories); Figure 10 OPs issued by sector 2014-June 2021 (all OP categories, percent by sector, sector labels garbled and not investor-specific: not taken); Premium Visa 510 approved (tourist long-stay visa, out of scope). Mandate to attract 50,000 retirees (added as target). Rest: economy, trade, manufacturing, financial services, governance, EDB financial statements (no permit fee revenue). Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

EDB residency portal page on the investor occupation permit (USD 100,000): minimum investment, 10-year validity, USD 1,000 permit fee from 11 July 2022 and USD 50 application fee from 1 Dec 2025 (both already in data), turnover conditions (MUR 5 million from year 3, MUR 8 million a year from year 5 for renewal), 60-day transfer deadline, PRP after 5 years with MUR 15 million a year or MUR 75 million over 5 years, dependants' permits, document lists. No statistics. Undated page. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

EDB residency portal page on the residence permit for retired non-citizens aged 50+: USD 2,000 a month or USD 24,000 a year, 10-year validity renewable, PRP after 5 consecutive years, USD 1,000 permit fee from 11 July 2022 (already in data), right to invest without employment, tax residence (183/270 days, general tax rule, not taken), dependants, document lists. No statistics. Undated page. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2017 (61 sections amending many Acts; mostly tax and other matters, not in scope). In scope: s. 25 Immigration Act (IHS buyers get resident status: event added; occupation permit for start-up investors, s. 9A(1A)); s. 29 Investment Promotion Act Schedule Part I new items 1E (USD 100,000 incl. high-tech equipment, USD 25,000 transfer) and 1F (USD 40,000 start-ups, 20% R&D) (terms added) and item 6 retired non-citizen USD 2,500 at issue and monthly (already in data); s. 41 Non-Citizens (Property Restriction) Act: retirees may acquire a lifetime right to live in a care home or similar unit outside smart cities (no amount); s. 61 commencement. Land duty and registration duty amendments have no scheme-specific rates. No statistics. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2020 (74 sections amending many Acts; mostly tax, customs, banking, other matters, not in scope). In scope: s. 16 EDB Act (new First Schedule in Third Schedule: criteria for investors, start-ups, food processing, film studio, other investors, professionals, young professionals, self-employed, retirees; PRP criteria Part II and pre-1 Sep 2020 Part III); s. 27 Immigration Act (USD 375,000 property residence incl. IRS/RES/IHS/PDS/SCS, PRP direct investment USD 375,000, permits 10 years, PRP 20 years, transitional PRP s. 5A(5AB), right of retirees to invest s. 9H); s. 45 Non-Citizens (Property Restriction) (Smart City serviced plots); s. 32 land duty references; s. 74 commencement (ss. 16(f) and 27 from 2 Sep 2020). Terms added for all investor and retiree criteria not already in data; professional and self-employed criteria (salaries, USD 35,000 self-employed) are not investment routes and were not taken. Two events added. Note: the existing FA 2020 terms and the property threshold event use 7 Aug 2020 (Act date) although s. 74(7) gives 2 Sep 2020. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2021 (97 sections amending many Acts; mostly tax, customs, finance and other matters, not in scope). In scope: s. 22 EDB Act (registration and deregistration rules incl. revocation of permits, Premium Investor Scheme for projects of MUR 500 million (business incentive, not residence), saving for pre-2006 investors, new First Schedule in the Fifth Schedule: investor USD 50,000 options and renewal income, retiree USD 1,500 a month or USD 18,000 a year, PRP criteria (USD 375,000; 3 years plus MUR 15 million; retiree USD 54,000), pre-Sept 2020 and pre-Oct 2006 criteria, Family Occupation Permit USD 250,000 to the COVID-19 Projects Development Fund (already in data)); s. 37 Immigration Act (G+2 apartments USD 375,000 and FOP s. 9CA: already in data with launch event; permits deemed approved after 5 working days; PRP 20 years; retiree PRP conversion USD 1,500 a month). Restated amounts identical to the 2020 schedule were not added again; the 2020 'film studio' and 'any other investor' items were dropped (valid_to set on those 2020 terms). s. 77 Registration Duty Act and s. 44 Land (Duties and Taxes) Act change IRS/RES/IHS duty references and delete USD 50,000/25,000 minimum-duty alternatives without printing the scheme rates (not taken). s. 62 Non-Citizens (Property Restriction) Act: EDB register of non-citizen property. Terms added: decision deadline, PRP conversion income, pre-2006 turnover, FOP validity. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Immigration Act 2022, replacing the 1970 Act. In scope: residence status for buyers of IRS/RES/IHS/PDS/Smart City property and G+2 apartments at USD 375,000 (alone or as each co-buyer's share) (s. 8); retiree permit (s. 10); permanent residence, 20-year validity, USD 1,500 monthly income to switch to retiree PRP (s. 11); investor occupation permit 10 years, 5-working-day deemed approval, extension of 3-year permits valid on 1 Sep 2020 (s. 12); family occupation permit 10 years (s. 14); transitional saving for IRS/RES owners (s. 39); consequential amendments to the EDB Act, Citizenship Act (s. 9(4) replaced: event added), and Non-Citizens (Property Restriction) Act (residents may buy other residential property from USD 350,000: purchase permission, no new residence route, not taken). Fees and deposits only 'as prescribed' (deposit up to MUR 100,000 applies to work-permit holders, not taken). Rest: admission, temporary residence for spouses, removal, offences (not in scope). Terms added; the Act's own event (2022-07-27) already in data. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

One-page MOTAC table of the four MM2H categories (Platinum, Gold, Silver, SEZ/SFZ by age): fixed deposit, pass term, minimum age, compulsory home purchase price, participating fee, processing fee, minimum days in Malaysia by age, fixed-deposit withdrawal, dependants (children to 35 and single; parents and in-laws allowed), tax exemption on foreign income and fixed-deposit profit, renewal fee. Fixed-deposit, home, participating and renewal fee terms were already in the data from this table; processing fees, pass terms, minimum ages, stay, withdrawal and child-age terms are added. The SEZ home price is 'as set for SEZ property development' (no amount). The only image is a logo. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

MOTAC MM2H 'Category Overview' web page (last update 10 Feb 2026): one table of requirements for Platinum, Gold, Silver and SEZ/SFZ (age 50+ and 21-49) categories: fixed deposit, term (20/15/5/10/10 years), minimum age, compulsory home purchase, participating fee, processing fee, minimum days per year, deposit withdrawal (max 50%), dependants (children up to 34), tax exemption, renewal fee. All amounts added as program_terms with this source (they repeat the categories page already in the data). SEZ/SFZ property price is 'as set for SEZ property development' (no number). The page's visitor counters are not about the programme. No statistics. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

One-page MOTAC announcement: the MM2H information management system (mm2h.gov.my/portal) is used for new applications from 1 August 2025, processing fee RM500 (excluding SST) per application, helpdesk number. Images are the ministry logo and a screenshot of the login page (OCR checked, msa+eng: no other content). The fee term and the event were already in the data; nothing new. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Written reply no. 159 (Oct-Dec 2019 sitting) by the Minister of Tourism, Arts and Culture: 39,295 applications received 2011-Sept 2019, 31,185 approved 2011-July 2019 from 131 countries, and an estimated RM18.3 billion contribution to the economy over 17 years (visa fees, fixed deposits, home purchases). The three amounts were already in the data; the number of nationalities (131) is added. No table. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Written text of oral reply no. 27 (4 Oct 2021, answered with no. 41) by the Home Minister on the revised MM2H: reactivation with applications handled by the Immigration Department from October 2021; nine new conditions (90 days' stay a year, offshore income RM40,000 a month instead of RM10,000, fixed deposit RM1 million with 50% withdrawal, age groups 35-49 and 50+ with RM50,000 extra deposit per dependant for the younger group, 5-year pass instead of 10, liquid assets RM1.5 million, pass fee RM500 a year instead of RM90, processing fee RM5,000 plus RM2,500 per dependant, security screening, good-conduct letter); policy changes (cap of 1% of Malaysian citizens, no low-skilled or security-sector applicants, monitoring, online system); 1-year conditional extension for existing participants; reasons, including the Auditor-General's report of 6 Oct 2020. Fixed deposit, income, liquid assets and fee terms and the announcement event were already in the data; stay, age, withdrawal, pass validity, cap and extension terms are added. The RM50,000 per dependant is already in the applies_to of the existing RM1 million fixed-deposit term. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Aanhangsel Handelingen II 2019/20 nr. 867 (8 pp.): 30 written questions by D66 MPs on Malta's passport sales and answers by the Foreign Minister and others (received 28 Nov 2019). Programme numbers: Malta (relayed from the ORiip report of Nov 2018): 961 'passports' issued to 1 Jul 2018 and a regional split of passport issuance 1 Jul 2015-1 Jul 2018 (Europe 266, Asia 70, Gulf 67, Africa 36, North America 20, Middle East 16, South America 4, Caribbean 3, Oceania 1; no total printed); the MPs' EUR 900,000 price; Netherlands investor scheme: fewer than 10 permits (already in the data), RVO added-value test (10 jobs within 5 years among three criteria), one-year review before abolition. Also the EC's count of member states with citizenship (3) and residence (20) schemes (lists, not programme numbers), Malta's due diligence, the Caruana Galizia inquiry, a Groningen professor (not named here), AIVD warnings. Added: 10 Malta rows (status reported), two terms, one event. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Staatsblad 2024 no. 83 (25 pp.): Decree of 9 Apr 2024 (published 16 Apr 2024, in force the next day) amending the Aliens Decree 2000, the Civic Integration Decree 2021 and the Foreign Nationals Employment Decree 2022, with explanatory note. Programme content: deletion of the residence ground for wealthy foreigners (art. 3.29a Vb 2000; Articles I B, D, G, II, III), transitional law keeping existing permits valid and renewable (Article IV), and the note's history (scheme from 1 Oct 2013, at least EUR 1,250,000 invested in an innovative company per Vc B11/2.2, fewer than ten permits granted). The rest (family reunification fraud checks, researcher mobility, mvv exemptions, EU directive fixes, detention hearings, consultation responses) is out of scope. The amount, the permit count and the launch were already in the data (the closure on 17 Apr 2024 is an event from another source); nothing new to add. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Gazette No. 36 (3 Feb 2026), SL 4 of 2026: Cabinet designates 'The Iruwa Initiative' special project (Cabinet resolution 29 Jan 2026) to mark the programme's first anniversary: main-applicant contribution cut from USD 115,000 to USD 90,000 from 29 Jan to 30 Jun 2026, other fees unchanged, applies to accepted applications not yet paid. Term and event already recorded; nothing else in it. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Gazette No. 197 (5 Jun 2026), SL 28 of 2026: Cabinet Resolution 539/2026 of 3 Jun 2026 extends the Iruwa Initiative to 31 Dec 2026. Term and event already recorded; nothing else in it. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Amendment Regulations No. 2 of 2026 (Gazette No. 32, certified 29 Jan 2026, 25 pp.): new definitions; agent forms; reg. 9A filing fees on submission, approval fees on approval in principle; police certificates (16+, six months' residence in past 10 years); new reg. 16 (Registrar endorsement, Minister, Cabinet); reg. 17 (approval fees within 30 days; agent fee and administration fee deducted from contribution); Part 4A electronic forms, lodgement (after 11:59 pm counts as next business day), signatures, notices, records; reg. 33 additional fees set by the Program Office; reg. 34 special projects; new Schedule 1 (application 5,000 + 2,000 per dependant; due diligence 6,000 / 3,000 / 3,000 benefactor; contribution 115,000 + 2,000 per dependant 16+ + 15,000 per sibling; passport 500); Schedule 2 (pre-approval additions); Schedule 3 (post-approval additions: application 5,000 each, due diligence 6,000, contributions 30,000 spouse, 0 child up to 2 and recently adopted child, 25,000 child 3-18 and grandchild, 35,000 others, passport 500); Schedule 4 (agent licence 5,000, agent fee 25,000); Schedule 4A (administration 10,000 / 5,000); Schedules 5-8 replaced by lists of required form contents (agent forms, application forms incl. 10-year address and employment history, oath, certificate, register). All schedule amounts and numeric rules now recorded (six were already there). Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Nauru Economic and Climate Resilience Citizenship Regulations 2024 (SL 28 of 2024, Gazette No. 453, 30 Oct 2024, 49 pp.; form pages 15-47 are images, read by OCR): eligibility and exclusions (police certificate for >6 months' residence in last 10 years; offences punishable by 12+ months; ICC, Interpol, terrorism, sanctions, high-risk-country citizens); approved due diligence firms, checks for 16+; agent licence (fee due 31 Jan, calendar-year licence, agent fee paid within 30 days of claim); application documents; 90-day verification; interviews 16+; dependants' affidavits (18+); Program Office -> Minister -> Registrar -> Cabinet; contribution and passport fees within 30 days of approval in principle; oath; certificate; post-approval additions; register access; Schedule 1 (contribution 105,000 / 110,000 / 115,000 / 15,000 per sibling; application fee 25,000 / 27,500 / 30,000; due diligence 10,000 / 7,500; passport 500), Schedule 2 (pre-approval additions: application 10,000, due diligence 7,500, passport 500, contribution to match family-size band), Schedule 3 (post-approval: contributions 25,000 spouse, 0 child up to 2 and recently adopted child, 20,000 child 3-18 and grandchild, 30,000 others; application fees 10,000 / 5,000 / 5,000 / 10,000 / 10,000 / 10,000; due diligence 7,500; passport 500), Schedule 4 (agent licence 5,000; agent fee 25,000); Schedules 5-8 forms: agent application (25% ownership disclosure), agent licence agreement and code of conduct (no advertising of agent fees, 30-day notice of sub-agents, no 'Nauru' in domain names), application information (fees non-refundable, contribution and passport fee paid on approval in principle), personal, financial and medical forms (10-year histories, five-year name-change bar), grant, oath, certificate and register templates. All amounts and numeric rules now recorded (eight terms were already there). Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Passports (Nauru Economic and Climate Resilience Citizenship Forms and Fees) Regulations 2025 (SL 26 of 2025, Gazette No. 201, notified 19 May 2025, 13 pp.): passport application for programme citizens (certificate of citizenship, 2 photos, foreign passport bio-page), passport contents (serial 'NN' + 6 digits), cancellation and lost/stolen notices (incl. cancellation under s. 25 of the 2024 Act), photo rules (4.5 x 3.5 cm, 70-80% face, not older than 3 months), separate register, records kept indefinitely; Schedule 3 fees: new passport USD 500, renewal USD 500 (already recorded as one term). Added the gazettal as an event. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

INZ visa information page (read 2 Oct 2026): cost from NZD 27470; processing time 80% of approvals in principle within 4 months; minimums NZD 5m Growth (36 months)/NZD 10m Balanced (60 months); acceptable investments by category, philanthropy max 20% for Growth; 6 months (plus possible 6) to transfer funds; days in NZ: 21 (Growth), 105 (Balanced) reduced by 14 days per extra NZD 1m in Growth investments (Table 1: 91/77/63 days); evidence at 24 and 36/60 months; resident travel 4/6 years; post-investment questionnaires; permanent residence after 36/60 months. Fees and minimums were already in program_terms; added presence, philanthropy cap, transfer deadline and processing time. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

MBIE briefing 2122-1943 (16 Dec 2021) with the 2022 proactive-release coversheet; pp. 2, 9 and 11 are images (OCR'd). Contents: recap of the Aug 2021 AIP design ($25m, weightings, bonds for 12 months, IELTS, up to 40% philanthropy, 88 days over three years), proposals to lower the threshold to $15m with a 3x weighting for direct investment and a 50% listed-equity cap (straw-person Annex One, Annex Two on Crown entities), and the note that INZ processed Investor 1 and 2 applications only to a decision-ready point during the border closure until the High Court ruling of 22 Nov 2021 (already an event). All figures are proposals that never applied as such (the adopted settings are recorded from the 2022 Cabinet minute); no statistics. Nothing new to add. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Oman Ministry of Foreign Affairs news page (29 Sep 2021, unofficial English translation): launch of the Investor Residency Programme by the commerce ministry; applications from 3 October; first 22 cards handed over; minister and OIA chairman quotes; first category (10 years: OMR 500,000 in shares of a joint-stock company or government bonds, or a company employing 50+ Omanis), second category (5 years: assets of OMR 250,000), retirees eligible, no citizenship entitlement; general investment incentives (100% foreign ownership, Invest-Easy portal with 1,500 activities and about 63,000 licences issued 4 Apr-27 Sep 2021). Taken: all programme numbers and rules (22 cards, the two thresholds and the launch event were already in the data; added the 50-employee route and the 10/5-year validity). Not taken (out of scope): Invest-Easy activity and licence counts (general business licensing, not the residence programme). Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Invest Oman blog post (Sept 2025) announcing the 10-Year Golden Residency: renewable 10-year residence for investors and families, seven investment routes (property in Integrated Tourism Complexes, company formation, Government Development Bonds, Muscat-listed shares, fixed-term bank deposit, business employing 50+ Omanis, nomination by a Foreign Capital Investment Law company), minimum capital OMR 200,000 (about USD 520,000), Migrate World as operational partner; general promotional material on Oman (share of global migrants targeting the Gulf over 10%, quality-of-life ranking 4th, access to 2.6 billion consumers). Taken: programme rules (the OMR 200,000 minimum and the launch event were already in the data; added 10-year validity and the 50-employee route). Not taken (out of scope): the general promotional statistics. The page links 21 images (not stored with the HTML, so not OCR-able here). Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Housing and Urban Planning Ministerial Decision 58/2022 (3 Mar 2022, Gazette 1433 of 13/3/2022; text via Qanoon.om): Art. 1 non-Omani investors may obtain a certificate of having bought residential units worth at least OMR 500,000 (first-category card) or OMR 250,000 (second category) in areas open to foreigners; Art. 2 first-category holders may own one residential, commercial or industrial property outside those areas (not in prohibited places); Art. 3 entry into force. Both thresholds and the event were already in the data; nothing else in scope. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Royal Oman Police Decision 234/2021 (21 Oct 2021; Gazette 1413 of 24/10/2021; text via Qanoon.om) amending the Foreign Residency Law regulations: investor visa (used within one year), dependants (spouse and first-degree relatives), conversion of visas, age exemption for investor dependants, residence of owners of units in integrated tourism complexes ends on disposal, fees: investor visas OMR 500 (10 years) and 300 (5 years), investor residence renewal OMR 500/300 every three years, dependant visas OMR 100/50 and dependant residence OMR 100/50 every three years, multiple-trip investor visa (up to one year, extendable, stays of up to three months). The two visa fees and the event were already in the data; added the renewal and dependant fees and the visa validity rules. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Gaceta Oficial 29643-A (13 Oct 2022), 9 pages. Pp. 1-4: contents page and Decreto Ejecutivo 54 of 2022 (Education, a school curriculum; out of scope; pp. 2-4 read by OCR). Pp. 5-8: Decreto Ejecutivo 109 of 13 Oct 2022 amending DE 722 (Qualified Investor): art. 1 rewrites art. 3 of DE 722 in full (real estate B/.500,000 free of liens, excess financeable by local mortgage, plus Registro Público and ANATI value certificates; presale contract B/.500,000 via local trust; securities B/.500,000 through a licensed broker on the Bolsa de Valores, held 5 years; fixed deposit B/.750,000 for at least 5 years at a general-licence bank), art. 2 extends the transitional B/.300,000 real-estate minimum from 24 to 48 months and keeps the 2020 Solvencia-to-Qualified-Investor switch, in force on promulgation. P. 9: an erratum to a Presidency decree naming a vice-minister (out of scope). No statistics. All amounts are already in the tables: the 48-month B/.300,000 term (t-c25007b41b), presale B/.500,000 (t-28252495dc) and event e-7e609f9061; the unchanged real-estate B/.500,000, securities B/.500,000 and deposit B/.750,000 restatements are recorded in the notes of the DE 722 terms (t-fce91dcfaf, t-5ea3c0dfe5, t-926941d879) rather than as duplicate rows. Note: art. 3 of DE 109 says it modifies only 'acápite a, numeral 2 del artículo 3', although art. 1 rewrites the whole of art. 3. Nothing new added in this pass. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Gaceta Oficial 30613 (16 Sept 2026), 41 pages; pp. 2-37 are scans read by OCR (spa+eng). Pp. 1-22 and 38-41: contents, Decretos 204 and 211 (appointments), DE 5 (environmental emergencies), DE 33 and 34 (Economy ministry) and commercial notices, all out of scope. No statistics. Route amounts, fees, deposit and naturalisation were already in the tables (t-2b6fc0b222, t-08807a143d, t-d0090088e5, t-0c2512386d, t-623ac85a5a, t-b1efe09d1b; fees noted on t-de6c73134f/t-3e97f07cc3; events e-3021dbfbd8, e-a1c0701293). This pass adds the art. 2 overall minimum, holding period, reinvestment window, processing maxima, certificate validity, new-dependant payments, the Solvencia switch event and an event listing the remaining procedural deadlines.
